note: File Download Counter is a submodule of file_download that logs per-file download counts (table file_download_counter with fid/totalcount/daycount/timestamp), gated by the file_download_counter.settings:count_downloads boolean, with Views field handlers and a 'Popular content' block (statistics_popular_block). IMPORTANT: this submodule declares core_version_requirement '^9 || ^10' and CANNOT be enabled on this Drupal 11 site — 'drush en file_download_counter' returns 'incompatible with this version of Drupal core'. Because it cannot be installed, there is no live config, DB table, block or Views field to introspect or mutate, so medium (introspection) and hard (execution) cases are intentionally omitted: they are not runnable on this environment and would fail every smoke test. The easy (recipe) cases below are grounded purely in the submodule's source (settings key, storage table, block/Views handlers) and require no site state.

evals.prompt: I installed the file_download_counter submodule but downloads are not being counted. Which configuration setting turns download counting on, and where is it set?
evals.expected_output: Enable the 'Count downloads' checkbox on the settings form at /admin/config/system/file-download-counter (route file_download_counter.settings, permission 'administer file download counter'). It is stored as file_download_counter.settings:count_downloads. When on, each download increments the file's counter.

evals.prompt: How does the file_download_counter module store download statistics, and which values does it keep per file?
evals.expected_output: It creates a database table named file_download_counter keyed by fid, with columns totalcount (all-time downloads), daycount (today's downloads, reset every 24h by cron) and timestamp (last download time). Each download runs file_download_counter_increment_file() to bump these.

evals.prompt: Once file_download_counter is tracking downloads, how can I display the counts to users — for example a list of the most downloaded content or a column in a View?
evals.expected_output: It provides two Views field handlers (a numeric download count and a last-download timestamp) so you can build a 'Top downloads' View, plus a 'Popular content' block (statistics_popular_block) showing today's / all-time / most-recently downloaded content (the block requires the count_content_views setting to be on).
